summaryForMax:
Feature: fixes the orbit-ring dead-zone/flicker bug Max found in his round-3 UAT dig (orrery-entry-orbits-2026-07-20) by replacing the old per-ring self-rendering SDF shader with one shared conic-math field pass (ringConic.js + OrbitConicField.js), then stripped the now-dead legacy renderer once the fix was proven live.

Unit layer: clean PASS. AC1 (the core conic math — 15/15 tests, real run) and AC11 (WebGL1-era dead code fully removed, string-pins consciously re-homed not dropped) both verified directly against real test output.

Integration layer: INSUFFICIENT, but not because anything looks broken. All 8 render-behavior ACs (AC2 dead-zone, AC3 far-orbit flicker, AC4 near-field, AC5 anti-vanish ladder, AC6 occlusion, AC7 parity, AC8 angular-size fade, AC9 single-pass perf) were already live-battery PASSed by chrome-devtools at commit 47ca81f/1a0bf9a (evidence/slice-d-live-battery.md). Since then, commit 3c46205 deleted the legacy SDF renderer entirely (the cleanup AC11 called for) — static diffs confirm the actual conic-render math is byte-unchanged and headless tests are still 1367/0 failed, so this is very likely still fine, but the archived battery's own A/B toggle mechanism no longer exists in code, so it can't formally stand in for a check at current HEAD (903d3d8). This is a working-Claude job, not yours: reopen chrome-devtools against 903d3d8, drive the lab's still-functional 'baseline' vs 'conic' modes (or live-game where the AC specifies it) for AC2–AC9, and confirm the same numbers hold.

UAT (AC10, yours alone — no agent can pass this): once integration is closed, load the game, go to Sol ORRERY, and check a near-field ring plus a grazing-angle pose. Look for: no double-lines, no flicker/dashing as you rotate through grazing angles, occlusion holding correctly behind planets. Two things are pre-flagged as expected-not-bugs, so don't dock them: the gentle-angle ring band now paints a bit wider than before, and the far-overview center cluster now reads as a solid dot rather than a tiny square. If those read fine to your eye and nothing else looks off, AC10 passes.
